extracted.intended_audience: data scientists, analysts, designers, and anyone creating data visualizations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing clear, truthful, and efficient data visualizations following Edward Tufte’s principles (maximize data-ink, minimize chartjunk, maintain graphical/contextual integrity). Intended to help practitioners choose charts, label them, and avoid common distortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-Ink Ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximize the proportion of ink that represents actual data versus total ink used in the graphic (Data-ink / Total ink).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a large share of ink dedicated to data; erase non-data-ink and redundant data-ink. Example removals: unnecessary gridlines, meaningless colors, 3D effects, and annotations that don’t add to the message. Aim to have ink change as the data change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Non-Data Ink (Minimize Chartjunk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce elements that do not convey data—decorations or extraneous graphical elements that distract from the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strip away visual clutter (chartjunk) such as heavy ornamentation, gratuitous decorations, and redundant marks. Treat redundant data-ink (elements that represent data but are excessive) as removable decoration. The goal is simplicity that preserves understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure visual representations are truthful and clear, avoiding practices that distort or misrepresent data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid misleading axes, inconsistent scales, truncated baselines, or other manipulations that exaggerate effects. Keep the lie factor close to 1 and ensure visuals reliably convey the intended message to support sound decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Zero Baseline (avoid when misleading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting an axis (usually the y-axis) at a value other than zero can exaggerate differences between data points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not start the y-axis at a non-zero baseline unless there is a justified reason; truncating the axis can make small changes seem large (e.g., starting at 90 instead of 0). If you must truncate, clearly indicate it and justify why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistent Scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Using different or non-uniform scales on axes can distort perceived relationships between variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent, uniform intervals on axes. Avoid mixing scales that make trends or relationships appear different than they truly are (e.g., non-uniform x-axis intervals or mismatched x/y scales).

rubrics_metrics.name: Slicing (pie chart overuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using too many slices in a pie chart makes interpretation difficult because small slices are hard to distinguish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pie charts with many categories; limit slices to a few meaningful parts or use an alternative display (bar chart, ordered dot plot) when categories are numerous or differences are subtle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant Data-Ink
rubrics_metrics.description: Marks that represent the data but are excessive and do not add new information (a form of non-data-ink).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove redundant encodings or repeated elements that do not increase understanding. Keep only the minimal marks needed to convey the measured quantities clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Create displays consistent with the information they represent and with the context/audience in which they will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete, balanced view of the data and consider audience needs (clarity, accuracy, accessibility). Account for color blindness, cultural context, and the decision-making context so the visualization supports correct interpretation and informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage Information Overload
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overwhelming viewers by presenting too much data at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small multiples, filtering, or focus+context techniques to highlight the most relevant information for the audience. Break complex information into digestible parts rather than a single dense display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure numbers and graphical elements are proportional to the quantities they measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design marks so visual area/length/position accurately reflects measured quantities. Avoid encodings or distortions that make visual magnitudes inconsistent with the underlying data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and Detailed Labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use precise, unambiguous labels to prevent graphical distortion and ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear axis labels, units, titles, and concise annotations. Labeling should eliminate guesswork about what is being measured and how; avoid vague or missing labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on Data Variation Over Design Variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize showing meaningful variation in the data itself rather than variation introduced by design choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let data variation drive the visualization; avoid decorative variations (colors, shapes, sizes) that draw attention away from actual differences in the data unless they encode meaningful information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Extra Dimensions (eschew unnecessary 3D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not add extra visual dimensions (e.g., 3D effects) unless they are necessary and informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 3D rendering or visual embellishments that do not add data value because they often obscure values and introduce visual distortion. Use the simplest dimensionality necessary to convey the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chart Choice (match chart to task)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select chart types appropriate to the data and the comparison or pattern you want to communicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bar charts for category comparisons, line charts for trends over time, and other appropriate encodings. Poor chart choice can obscure the message—pick the form that best reveals the question of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace and Layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Use whitespace and separation to reduce clutter and make multiple elements easier to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adequate spacing between charts and elements to avoid visual crowding. Whitespace helps viewers separate sections and follow the narrative of the visualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Use of Color
rubrics_metrics.description: Use color selectively to distinguish or highlight information without adding confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose palettes with clear distinctions, accessible color choices (for color blindness), and semantic or consistent mappings. Avoid decorative colors that don’t map to data meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure visuals provide sufficient context so data are interpreted correctly and balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include necessary contextual information (timeframe, units, sample sizes, sources). A chart stripped of context can mislead even if visually tidy—balance simplicity with completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lie Factor (honest magnitude representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the lie factor close to 1 so the visual magnitude of change reflects the real magnitude of change in the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid scaling or visual encodings that inflate or deflate perceived effects relative to actual data. If non-standard encoding is used, disclose and justify it.
